teile.einleitung: Fondue is a well-known Swiss dish made of melted cheese. You dip pieces of bread on a long fork into the hot cheese. The “moitié moitié” fondue from the canton of Fribourg is especially popular.
wichtigste: Fondue is made from melted cheese.
It is eaten together from one pot, the caquelon.
Pieces of bread are dipped into the cheese on a long fork.
“Moitié moitié” means “half and half”.
This fondue is made from Gruyère and Vacherin fribourgeois.
Fondue is regarded as a national dish of Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The word **fondue** comes from the French “fondre”, which means “to melt”. For a cheese fondue, cheese is melted together with white wine, garlic and a little starch. Often a splash of kirsch is added. The mixture is stirred until it is nice and creamy. For children, the wine can be replaced with other liquids.

Fondue is served in a special pot, the **caquelon**. It is usually made of ceramic or cast iron. The pot stands on a **rechaud**, a small burner, so that the cheese stays warm and runny. Everyone sits around the table and dips their pieces of bread in on a long **fondue fork**. It is best to stir the pot a little all the time.

In the **canton of Fribourg**, the “**moitié moitié**” fondue is very popular. In French this means “half and half”. For it you use half **Gruyère** and half **Vacherin fribourgeois**. Both kinds of cheese come from the canton of Fribourg. There is also a fondue made only from Vacherin, which is prepared with water instead of wine.

In the past, fondue was mainly eaten in the mountain regions. In the 20th century, the Swiss cheese industry made it known all over the country. Today it is regarded as a **national dish** and is especially enjoyed in winter. In many families there is a funny custom: anyone who loses their bread in the pot has to do a small task.

gewusst: The crispy crust of cheese that is left at the bottom of the caquelon at the end is called “la religieuse”.
In Switzerland there are many regional fondue mixtures, depending on which cheeses there are in the area.

teile.einleitung: Lake Geneva is a large lake in the west of Switzerland. It lies between Switzerland and France. Well-known cities such as Geneva, Lausanne and Montreux lie on its shores.
wichtigste: In French, Lake Geneva is called “Lac Léman”.
It is the largest lake in Switzerland, but Switzerland shares it with France.
The northern shore belongs to Switzerland, and a large part of the southern shore to France.
The city of Geneva lies at the south-western end of the lake.
Lausanne lies on the northern shore.
The Rhône flows through the lake.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Geneva** is called **Lac Léman** in French. It is shaped like a crescent moon. With an area of about 580 square kilometres, it is one of the largest lakes in central Europe. The northern shore belongs to **Switzerland**, and a large part of the southern shore to **France**. The cantons of **Geneva**, **Vaud** and **Valais** border Lake Geneva.

The city of **Geneva** lies at the **south-western end** of the lake. The famous **Jet d'eau**, a huge fountain of water, stands there. **Lausanne** lies on the **northern shore** and climbs steeply up the slope from the lake. Further east come **Vevey** and **Montreux**. At Montreux, **Chillon Castle** stands right on the water.

The **Rhône** comes from the Valais and flows into the lake at Villeneuve. It leaves the lake again in Geneva and flows on to France. At its deepest point, Lake Geneva is over 300 metres deep. Because it holds so much water, it also influences the **climate**: on the shore it is often milder than in the surrounding area.

On the northern shore between Lausanne and Vevey lie the steep vineyards of **Lavaux**. Since 2007 they have been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Old **paddle steamers**, which are already over a hundred years old, sail on the lake. In summer, many people swim, sail or row on Lake Geneva.

gewusst: The biggest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland is not Lake Geneva but Lake Neuchâtel.
The Jet d'eau in Geneva shoots water about 140 metres into the air.

teile.einleitung: The Glacier Express is a famous panoramic train through the Swiss Alps. It runs from Zermatt in the Valais to St Moritz in the canton of Graubünden and is known as the slowest express train in the world.
wichtigste: The Glacier Express runs between Zermatt and St Moritz.
The journey takes about eight hours.
It has been running since 1930.
It crosses many bridges and goes through many tunnels.
The highest point is the Oberalp Pass at 2,033 metres.
It is known as the slowest express train in the world.

abschnitte.text: The **Glacier Express** links two well-known holiday resorts: **Zermatt** in the canton of Valais and **St Moritz** in the canton of Graubünden. On the way it also passes through the canton of Uri. The journey takes about **eight hours**. The train has been running since **1930**. Its name means “glacier express” because in the past you could see the Rhône Glacier on the way.

The Glacier Express is often called the **slowest express train in the world**. It runs on a narrow gauge, the **metre gauge**, through steep terrain. That is why it only makes slow progress. But this is intended: passengers have enough time to enjoy the landscape. The carriages have large **panoramic windows** that reach up into the roof.

On the route, the train crosses almost **300 bridges** and goes through about **90 tunnels**. The highest point is the **Oberalp Pass** at **2,033 metres**. Especially famous is the **Landwasser Viaduct** in Graubünden, a tall stone bridge that leads straight into a tunnel in the rock face. The Albula line with this viaduct is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

The Glacier Express is run by two railway companies: the **Matterhorn Gotthard Railway** and the **Rhaetian Railway**. On the way you see mountains, glaciers, gorges and small mountain villages. In Zermatt the journey begins at the foot of the **Matterhorn**. In St Moritz it ends in the Engadine.

gewusst: The Glacier Express takes about eight hours for the route, which is around 290 kilometres long.
The Landwasser Viaduct is about 65 metres high and leads straight into a tunnel in the rock.

teile.einleitung: The Hammetschwand Lift is a lift on the Bürgenstock in the canton of Nidwalden. It runs up the outside of a steep rock face and is regarded as the highest outdoor lift in Europe. It opened as early as 1905.
wichtigste: The Hammetschwand Lift stands on the Bürgenstock in Nidwalden.
It goes up the outside of a rock face.
It is regarded as the highest outdoor lift in Europe.
It opened in 1905.
At the top you have a wide view over Lake Lucerne.
The spectacular Felsenweg (“rock path”) leads to the lift.

abschnitte.titel: A lift on the rock face
abschnitte.text: Most lifts run inside a building. The **Hammetschwand Lift**, however, runs up the **outside** of a vertical rock face. The cabin glides about 150 metres upwards in a steel frame. Through the windows you look far down to the lake during the ride. At the top you reach the summit of the **Hammetschwand**, the highest point of the Bürgenstock.

The lift opened in **1905**. It belonged to a large hotel area that businessmen had built up on the **Bürgenstock**. It was meant to be a special attraction for guests from all over the world. Later the lift was modernised so that it now runs safely and quickly.

You reach the lift along the **Felsenweg**. This path was cut into the steep rock face and runs high above **Lake Lucerne**. In places it goes through small tunnels. From the top station you can see across the lake, to Lucerne and as far as the Alps.

gewusst: The Bürgenstock lies between the cantons of Nidwalden and Lucerne, right on Lake Lucerne.
A funicular railway also runs up to the Bürgenstock, starting at a boat landing on the lake.

teile.einleitung: The Hauenstein Base Tunnel is a railway tunnel through the Jura. It runs from Tecknau in the canton of Basel-Landschaft to Olten in the canton of Solothurn. Since 1916 it has been an important link between Basel and the Central Plateau.
wichtigste: The Hauenstein Base Tunnel runs from Tecknau (BL) to Olten (SO).
It opened in 1916.
It is about 8 kilometres long.
It passes under the ridges of the Jura.
It replaced the older, higher Hauenstein summit tunnel.
Many trains between Basel and Bern or Zurich go through it.

abschnitte.text: Between **Basel** and the **Central Plateau** lies the **Jura**, a long chain of hills and mountains. For the railway this is an obstacle, because trains cannot climb steep slopes. That is why tunnels were built through the mountain. The **Hauenstein** is a pass in the Jura over which roads have led since ancient times.

As early as the 19th century, the **Hauenstein summit tunnel** was built near Läufelfingen. It lies higher up in the mountain, and the trains had to climb a steep ramp. This was slow and hard work for the locomotives. As traffic grew, a new tunnel at a lower level became necessary.

The **Hauenstein Base Tunnel** opened in **1916**. It lies lower and is therefore flatter than the old tunnel. It begins at **Tecknau** in the canton of Basel-Landschaft and ends at **Olten**. Since then, most express trains and freight trains between Basel and the Central Plateau have used it. This makes Olten one of the most important railway junctions in Switzerland.

gewusst: The name “base tunnel” means that a tunnel lies low down at the foot of a mountain.
Regional trains still use the old summit tunnel.

teile.einleitung: The Helvetic Republic was a state on the territory of present-day Switzerland from 1798 to 1803. It came about after French troops marched in. Its first capital, for a short time, was Aarau in what is now the canton of Aargau.
wichtigste: The Helvetic Republic existed from 1798 to 1803.
It came about after the French invasion.
Its first capital was briefly Aarau, then Lucerne and later Bern.
It was a unitary state with a single government.
The cantons lost a large part of their power.
In 1803 Napoleon ended it with the Act of Mediation.

abschnitte.titel: The end of the old Confederation
abschnitte.text: Before 1798, Switzerland was a loose alliance of states, the **Old Swiss Confederacy**. Many people in subject territories had few rights. After the **French Revolution**, new ideas of freedom and equality spread. In 1798, **French troops** marched into Switzerland, and the old order collapsed.

Following the example of France, the **Helvetic Republic** came into being. It was a **unitary state**: there was a single government, a constitution and a parliament for the whole country. The **cantons** became administrative districts with no power of their own. All citizens were to be equal before the law, and the subject territories were freed.

In **1798**, the town of **Aarau** became the first capital of the Helvetic Republic. The government and parliament met there. But after only a few months, the government moved to **Lucerne** and later to **Bern**. Aarau is therefore proud of having been the first capital of Switzerland for a short time.

Many people, especially in central Switzerland, rejected the new state. They wanted their old rights and the independence of the cantons back. There was fierce **conflict** between supporters and opponents. In 1803, **Napoleon** issued the **Act of Mediation**. With it, the cantons regained more rights, and the Helvetic Republic came to an end.

gewusst: New cantons later grew out of areas of the Helvetic period, such as Aargau, Thurgau, St Gallen, Ticino and Vaud, which became independent in 1803.
In the Helvetic Republic, a single currency for the whole country, the franc, was introduced for the first time.

teile.einleitung: Flüeli-Ranft is a small place in the canton of Obwalden. Niklaus von Flüe, known as Brother Klaus, lived here for many years as a hermit in a gorge. Today the place is a well-known place of pilgrimage.
wichtigste: Flüeli-Ranft belongs to the municipality of Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden.
Flüeli is a village, and the Ranft is a gorge below it.
Niklaus von Flüe lived as a hermit in the Ranft from 1467.
He is called Brother Klaus.
He is regarded as the patron saint of Switzerland.
He was declared a saint in 1947.

abschnitte.text: **Flüeli** is a small village above Lake Sarnen and belongs to the municipality of **Sachseln**. Below the village lies the **Ranft**, a wooded gorge with the stream Grosse Melchaa. A steep path leads down from the village into the gorge. There you will find a small chapel and the cell of Brother Klaus.

**Niklaus von Flüe** was born in 1417. He was a farmer, had a large family and was also a judge and councillor in Obwalden. In **1467**, with the agreement of his wife Dorothea, he left his family. He withdrew to the Ranft and lived there for about twenty years as a **hermit**. He prayed a lot, and it is said that he ate nothing during this time.

Many people came to Brother Klaus to ask him for advice. In **1481**, the Confederate states were arguing fiercely with each other. Advice from Brother Klaus helped them to agree on the **Covenant of Stans** (“Stanser Verkommnis”). In this way, a war between the Confederates was avoided. That is why he is still seen as a peacemaker today.

Brother Klaus died in 1487. In **1947**, the Catholic Church **declared him a saint**. He is regarded as the **patron saint** of Switzerland. Every year many pilgrims visit Flüeli-Ranft. His grave is in the church of Sachseln.

gewusst: In the village of Flüeli you can still visit the house where Brother Klaus was born and the house where he lived.
Brother Klaus is also valued as a role model by many Protestant Christians.

teile.einleitung: The Gotthard Rail Tunnel is the first railway tunnel through the Gotthard. It runs from Göschenen in the canton of Uri to Airolo in Ticino and opened in 1882. At that time it was a masterpiece of engineering and made the journey through the Alps much faster.
wichtigste: The Gotthard railway tunnel opened in 1882.
It is about 15 kilometres long.
It connects Göschenen (UR) with Airolo (TI).
It is also called the summit tunnel, because it lies high in the mountain.
Construction took about ten years and was very dangerous.
The engineer Louis Favre led the building work.

abschnitte.titel: A tunnel for the Gotthard Railway
abschnitte.text: In the 19th century, many railways were built in Europe. The **Gotthard Railway** was meant to link the north with Italy. The biggest obstacle was the Gotthard massif. That is why a tunnel about 15 kilometres long was built between **Göschenen** and **Airolo**. It opened in **1882**.

From **1872**, workers dug into the mountain from both sides. They drilled holes in the rock and blasted it with **dynamite**. The work was hard, hot and dusty, and many workers lost their lives in accidents. Most of the workers came from Italy. The engineer **Louis Favre** led the building work, but died in 1879, shortly before the two sides met.

abschnitte.titel: Spiral tunnels and a little church
abschnitte.text: So that the train could climb up to the tunnel, **spiral tunnels** were built. In these tunnels the train goes round in a circle through the mountain and gains height as it does so. Near **Wassen** in the canton of Uri you therefore see the church three times from different angles. The “Chileli vo Wasse” (the little church of Wassen) is very well known for this.

Since the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** has existed, most trains go through the new tunnel down below. Mainly regional trains and day trippers still use the old **mountain line**. Many people use the line because it is very beautiful. The old tunnel is an important piece of Swiss transport history.

gewusst: When it opened, the Gotthard Rail Tunnel was the longest tunnel in the world.
The Zurich politician and businessman Alfred Escher drove the building of the Gotthard Railway forward strongly.

t13w50if.t: Grand Council of the Canton of Thurgau

teile.einleitung: The Grand Council is the parliament of the canton of Thurgau. It makes the laws of the canton and decides on money. What is special is that it meets alternately in two places: in Frauenfeld and in Weinfelden.
wichtigste: The Grand Council is the cantonal parliament of Thurgau.
It has 130 members.
In the summer half of the year it meets in Frauenfeld, in the winter half in Weinfelden.
This arrangement is unusual in Switzerland.
The members are elected by the people every four years.
The government of the canton is called the Regierungsrat (Government Council).

abschnitte.titel: What does a cantonal parliament do?
abschnitte.text: Every canton has a **parliament** of its own. In Thurgau it is called the **Grand Council**. The members discuss and pass **laws** that apply in the whole canton. They also decide on the **budget**, that is, on what the canton spends its money on. They also keep a check on the work of the government.

The Grand Council does not always meet in the same place. In the **summer half of the year** it meets in **Frauenfeld**, the main town of the canton. In the **winter half of the year** it meets in **Weinfelden**. Weinfelden lies roughly in the middle of the canton. This arrangement is old and unique in Switzerland.

The **130 members** of the Grand Council are elected by the people of Thurgau, every **four years**. They belong to different **parties**. Most of them do this work alongside their jobs, which is known as the **militia system**. In this way, farmers, teachers, business owners and many others bring their experience to the work.

Besides the parliament there is the **government**, called the **Regierungsrat** in Thurgau. It has five members and runs the administration of the canton. The parliament makes the laws, and the government carries them out. Important decisions can also be put to the people in a **vote**.

gewusst: Weinfelden is not the main town, but it is home to the cantonal parliament in winter.
In other cantons the parliament is called, for example, the Kantonsrat, Landrat or Grosser Rat.

teile.einleitung: The Hoher Kasten is a mountain in the Alpstein in Appenzell Innerrhoden. On its summit there is a revolving restaurant that moves slowly in a circle. From there you can see into the Rhine valley, to Lake Constance and to the mountains.
wichtigste: The Hoher Kasten lies in the Alpstein in Appenzell Innerrhoden.
It is just under 1,800 metres high.
A cable car runs from Brülisau to the summit.
At the top there is a revolving restaurant.
You can see into the Rhine valley, to Lake Constance and as far as Austria.
A geology walking trail explains how the mountains were formed.

abschnitte.text: The **Hoher Kasten** is part of the **Alpstein**, the mountain range in the Appenzell region. It lies on the border between the cantons of Appenzell Innerrhoden and St Gallen. From **Brülisau**, a **cable car** goes to the summit in a few minutes. If you like walking, you can also climb up on foot.
On the summit there is a **revolving restaurant**. The floor with the tables turns slowly in a circle. This way, while you eat, you gradually see in all directions without getting up.

To the east, the mountain drops steeply into the **Rhine valley**. The Rhine flows there, and on the other side lies **Austria**. To the north, **Lake Constance** glitters, and to the south you can see the Säntis and many other peaks. In clear weather the view reaches very far.

From the Hoher Kasten, a **geology walking trail** leads along the ridge towards the Saxer Lücke. Signs explain how the Alpstein was formed. The rocks were laid down in the sea long ago and later folded up into mountains. That is why you sometimes find fossils of sea animals in the **limestone**.

gewusst: The rock of the Alpstein was originally laid down on the floor of a sea.
At 2,502 metres, the Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein.

teile.einleitung: Heiden is a village in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. It lies high above Lake Constance and offers a wide view as far as Germany and Austria. Heiden is also known as the home of Henry Dunant, the founder of the Red Cross.
wichtigste: Heiden lies in Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
From the village you can see across Lake Constance.
Germany and Austria lie on the other shore.
Henry Dunant spent the last years of his life in Heiden.
After a fire in the 19th century, the village was rebuilt in the Biedermeier style.
A rack railway links Heiden with Rorschach on the lake.

abschnitte.text: Heiden lies on a terrace in the **Appenzell Vorderland**, about 800 metres above sea level. **Lake Constance** spreads out below. On the opposite shore lie **Germany** and **Austria**. In clear weather you can see far across the water. This beautiful location made Heiden well known early on.

abschnitte.titel: A village in the Biedermeier style
abschnitte.text: In **1838**, a fire destroyed a large part of the village. After that, Heiden was rebuilt in the style of the time, the **Biedermeier** style. The houses are light, plain and neatly arranged. That is why the village centre still looks very uniform today and is protected.

In the 19th century, Heiden became a popular **health resort**. Visitors from many countries came to recover in the fresh air. They drank, for example, **whey**, the liquid left over when cheese is made, because it was thought to be healthy. Hotels and walking paths were built for the visitors.

**Henry Dunant** of Geneva lived in Heiden from 1887 and died here in 1910. He had co-founded the **Red Cross** and in 1901 received the first **Nobel Peace Prize**. In Heiden, the **Henry Dunant Museum** recalls his life. The village is therefore a special place for people from all over the world.

gewusst: The rack railway from Rorschach to Heiden has been running since 1875.
Three countries meet on Lake Constance: Switzerland, Germany and Austria.

teile.einleitung: The Gornergrat Railway is a rack railway in the canton of Valais. Since 1898 it has run from Zermatt up to the Gornergrat at over 3,000 metres. From the top you can see the Matterhorn and many glaciers.
wichtigste: The Gornergrat Railway runs from Zermatt to the Gornergrat.
It opened in 1898.
It was the first electrically powered rack railway in Switzerland.
The top station lies at over 3,000 metres above sea level.
From the Gornergrat you can see the Matterhorn, Monte Rosa and the Gorner Glacier.

abschnitte.text: Normal trains can only manage gentle slopes, otherwise the wheels slip. A **rack railway** therefore has a **rack rail** between the rails. A cogwheel on the train grips this rail and pulls the train safely uphill. On the way down, too, the cogwheel brakes reliably. This is how the Gornergrat Railway can climb steep slopes.

The Gornergrat Railway opened in **1898**. It ran on **electricity** from the start and was therefore the first electric rack railway in Switzerland. At that time this was modern technology. The line leads from **Zermatt** through forests and over alpine pastures right up into a world of rock and ice.

The **Gornergrat** is a rocky ridge above the **Gorner Glacier**. From there you can see the **Matterhorn** and **Monte Rosa** with the Dufourspitze, the highest peak in Switzerland. All around stand many more four-thousand-metre peaks. At the top there is a hotel with two observatory towers.

The starting point, **Zermatt**, is a **car-free** village. Visitors arrive by train and get around the village on foot or in small electric vehicles. The Gornergrat Railway runs all year round. In winter it also takes skiers up to the ski area.

gewusst: The Gornergrat Railway is regarded as the highest open-air rack railway in Europe.
At 4,634 metres, the Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is the highest mountain in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Estavayer-le-Lac is a pretty little town in the canton of Fribourg. It lies on the southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel and is known for its well-preserved medieval old town.
wichtigste: Estavayer-le-Lac lies on the southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel.
The little town belongs to the canton of Fribourg.
French is spoken here.
The old town largely dates from the Middle Ages.
Chenaux Castle is the best-known building.
Since 2017, Estavayer-le-Lac has been part of the larger municipality of Estavayer.

abschnitte.text: Estavayer-le-Lac lies on **Lake Neuchâtel**, the largest lake that lies entirely within Switzerland. The little town is on the southern shore, in the Broye district of the canton of Fribourg. The name gives it away: “le Lac” means “the lake” in French. From the shore you can look across the water to the hills of the Jura.

The old town with its narrow lanes, arcades and old houses is very well preserved. Especially well known is **Chenaux Castle**, a medieval castle with thick walls and towers. Today it houses offices. The big collegiate church of Saint Laurence also shapes the look of the town. Anyone strolling through the lanes feels a little as if they had been taken back to another time.

In Estavayer-le-Lac there is an unusual **Frog Museum**. It shows stuffed frogs that are arranged like people in scenes from everyday life, for example playing cards. The collection was made in the 19th century. The museum also shows objects from the history of the little town.

In summer, many people come to the lake for swimming, sailing and other **water sports**. The shore is flat and in many places lined with reeds. This shore zone is an important habitat for birds. In this way, Estavayer-le-Lac combines history, nature and leisure.

gewusst: In the Frog Museum in Estavayer-le-Lac, stuffed frogs act out scenes from everyday life.
The southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel is one of the largest reed and wetland areas in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Frauenfeld is the main town of the canton of Thurgau. It is also the largest town in the canton and lies on the Murg in north-eastern Switzerland.
wichtigste: Frauenfeld is the main town of the canton of Thurgau.
It is also the largest town in Thurgau.
Kreuzlingen on Lake Constance follows closely behind.
The town lies on the river Murg.
Its landmark is Frauenfeld Castle.
The big music festival Openair Frauenfeld is also well known.

abschnitte.text: **Frauenfeld** is the **main town** of the canton of **Thurgau**. The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament, the Grand Council, meet here. Frauenfeld is also the **largest town** in the canton. **Kreuzlingen** on Lake Constance follows closely behind. Thurgau has no really big cities, but many smaller towns and villages.

In the middle of the old town stands **Frauenfeld Castle** with a mighty medieval tower. Today it houses the **Thurgau Historical Museum**. The old town lies on a rise above the river **Murg**. The town's coat of arms shows a woman and a lion.

Every summer, **Openair Frauenfeld** takes place, one of the biggest hip-hop festivals in Europe. Then tens of thousands of music fans come to the big meadow, the **Grosse Allmend**. **Horse races** are also held there. The Swiss Army also has an important military training area in Frauenfeld.

Around Frauenfeld there are many fields, meadows and **fruit trees**. Because of its many apple trees, Thurgau is sometimes called “Mostindien” (“Cider India”). Frauenfeld is well connected to Zurich and Winterthur by train. Many people therefore live here and work in the larger cities.

gewusst: Because of its many apple trees and its cider, Thurgau is jokingly called “Mostindien”.
Frauenfeld is only a little bigger than Kreuzlingen, the second largest town in Thurgau.

teile.einleitung: The Einsiedeln World Theatre is a large open-air theatre in Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz. It is performed on the square in front of the monastery, and hundreds of people from the village take part.
wichtigste: The World Theatre is performed in Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It is played in the open air on the monastery square.
The first performance took place in 1924.
It is only performed every few years.
Hundreds of amateur actors from Einsiedeln take part.
The idea goes back to a Spanish play from the 17th century.

abschnitte.text: The **Einsiedeln World Theatre** is an **open-air theatre**. That means it is performed outdoors. The stage is the large square in front of the **monastery church** of Einsiedeln. The magnificent façade of the monastery forms the backdrop. Thousands of spectators sit on stands in front of it.

The idea comes from the Spanish poet **Pedro Calderón de la Barca**. In the 17th century he wrote the play **“The Great Theatre of the World”**. In it, people play their roles in life as if on a stage, for example as a king, a farmer or a beggar. At the end, the play asks how each person has played their role.

What is special is that mostly **amateurs** from Einsiedeln take part. Amateurs are people who do not act as their job. Hundreds of children, teenagers and adults help on stage, with sewing the costumes or behind the scenes. For the village, the World Theatre is therefore a big celebration that everyone shares.

The first performance took place in **1924**. Since then, the World Theatre has not been performed every year, but at **longer intervals**. In more recent times, Swiss authors have reworked the play. This way it also fits the questions of our own time.

gewusst: At the Einsiedeln World Theatre, the façade of a real monastery church is the scenery.
The idea for the play is almost 400 years old.

teile.einleitung: The Fraumünster is a well-known church in the old town of Zurich. Its coloured glass windows, designed by the artist Marc Chagall, are world famous.
wichtigste: The Fraumünster stands in Zurich on the Limmat.
It was founded as a convent in the year 853.
The abbesses of the convent were very powerful for a long time.
During the Reformation, the last abbess handed the convent over to the city.
Marc Chagall made five glass windows in the choir around 1970.
Today the Fraumünster is a Reformed church.

abschnitte.text: The Fraumünster was founded in the year **853**. King **Louis the German** gave the convent to his daughter Hildegard, who became the first **abbess**. An abbess is the head of a convent. That is why the church is called “Frau”münster (“Women's Minster”). It stands on the Limmat, opposite the Grossmünster.

In the Middle Ages, the abbesses of the Fraumünster were very **influential**. For a long time, for example, they were allowed to have **coins** minted. During the **Reformation**, the last abbess, **Katharina von Zimmern**, handed the convent over to the city of Zurich in 1524. In this way she prevented conflict and violence. Since then, the Fraumünster has been a Reformed church.

Around **1970**, the artist **Marc Chagall** designed five large **glass windows** in the choir of the church. They glow in strong colours such as blue, green, red and yellow. The pictures show stories from the Bible. Chagall was already over 80 years old at the time. Many visitors come to Zurich specially to see these windows.

In the Fraumünster there is also a large glass window by the Swiss artist **Augusto Giacometti**. It dates from the 1940s. The church's **organ** is also well known and is played at concerts. With its pointed green tower, the Fraumünster is part of the picture of Zurich's old town.

gewusst: Chagall came from what is now Belarus and was already over 80 when he worked on the Zurich windows.
In the Middle Ages, the abbesses of the Fraumünster were so powerful that they had their own coins minted.

teile.einleitung: Georg Fischer, GF for short, is a large industrial company from Schaffhausen. Today the firm is mainly known for piping systems and operates worldwide.
wichtigste: Georg Fischer was founded in Schaffhausen.
The firm still has its headquarters there today.
Its beginnings go back to the year 1802.
The abbreviation is GF.
Today GF is mainly known for piping systems.
The company operates in many countries around the world.

abschnitte.text: The history of the company begins in **1802** in **Schaffhausen**. At that time, **Johann Conrad Fischer** founded a workshop where metal was worked. Later it grew into a large **foundry**. In a foundry, liquid metal is poured into moulds. The firm was named **Georg Fischer** after a member of the family.

Today GF is mainly known for **piping systems**. These are pipes, connectors and valves through which, for example, **water** or **gas** flows. Many of them are made of **plastic**. They are needed in houses, factories and for the water supply of cities. GF also makes other technical products.

Georg Fischer still has its **headquarters** in **Schaffhausen** today. But the company has factories and branches in many countries. It employs thousands of people around the world. For the town of Schaffhausen, GF is an important **employer**. The firm is listed on the Swiss stock exchange.

gewusst: Georg Fischer is over 200 years old, which makes it one of the oldest industrial firms in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Hölloch is a huge cave in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz. With over 200 kilometres of passages, it is one of the longest cave systems in the world.
wichtigste: The Hölloch lies in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz.
The known passages are over 200 kilometres long altogether.
It is one of the longest cave systems in the world.
The cave was formed in limestone, and water shaped the passages.
Researchers are still discovering new parts.
In heavy rain, passages can suddenly be flooded.

abschnitte.text: The Hölloch is not a single chamber, but a huge **cave system** with passages on many levels. The surveyed passages are over 200 kilometres long altogether. This makes the Hölloch one of the longest caves in the world and one of the longest in Europe. There are narrow crawl spaces, steep shafts and big halls. Inside it is dark and cool all year round.

The Hölloch lies in **limestone**. Rainwater contains a little carbonic acid and can slowly dissolve lime. Over a very long time, the water has in this way widened cracks in the rock into passages. Water still flows through the cave today. After heavy rain or during the snowmelt, it sometimes rises quickly and fills whole passages.

In the 19th century, a farmer from the Muota valley began to explore the cave. Later, **cave explorers** studied it more closely and surveyed the passages. In 1952, a group of explorers was caught by floodwater and had to wait for several days in the cave until they could get out again. Today research groups with good equipment are out and about and are still finding new passages.

A small part of the Hölloch can be visited on **guided tours**. For this you need warm clothes, good shoes and a lamp. Longer tours take many hours, some even with a night in the cave. You should never go in alone, because it is easy to get lost and the water can become dangerous.

gewusst: For a long time, the Hölloch was regarded as the longest known cave in the world.
In the depths of the Hölloch there is no time of day: it is always completely dark.

teile.einleitung: The Engelberger Aa is a river in central Switzerland. It comes from the valley of Engelberg, flows through Nidwalden and runs into Lake Lucerne at Buochs.
wichtigste: The Engelberger Aa comes from the valley of Engelberg.
It flows through the canton of Nidwalden.
At Buochs it flows into Lake Lucerne.
The old word “Aa” simply means water or river.
In storms it can carry dangerous floodwater.

abschnitte.titel: From the mountain to the lake
abschnitte.text: The **Engelberger Aa** collects its water in the mountains around **Engelberg** in Obwalden. Then it flows down through the **Engelberg valley** into the canton of **Nidwalden**. It passes places such as **Wolfenschiessen** and **Dallenwil**. At **Buochs** it flows into **Lake Lucerne**.

The word **Aa** is very old and simply means **water** or **river**. There are several rivers with this name in Switzerland. So people add where the river comes from, which gives “Engelberger Aa”. Other streams in the region are also called Aa.

After heavy rain, the Engelberger Aa can carry a great deal of water. In **2005**, a major **flood** caused serious damage in Nidwalden. Afterwards the **embankments** were strengthened and new protective measures were built. This is meant to protect villages and fields better in future.

gewusst: In Switzerland there are several rivers that are simply called “Aa”, because the word used to mean water.

teile.einleitung: The EPFL is the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, in the canton of Vaud. It belongs to the Confederation and is the French-speaking sister of ETH Zurich.
wichtigste: EPFL stands for École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne.
In English it is called the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne.
It lies near Lausanne, right on Lake Geneva.
Since 1969 it has been a university of the Confederation.
Together with ETH Zurich it belongs to the ETH Domain.
People from many countries study and do research there.

abschnitte.text: The **EPFL** is one of two **technical universities** that belong to the **Confederation**. The other is **ETH Zurich**. Together with several research institutes, they form the **ETH Domain**. At the EPFL, teaching is mainly in **French** and English.

The school began in the 19th century as a small private **school of engineering** in Lausanne. Later it was part of the **University of Lausanne**. In **1969**, the Confederation took over the school, and it became the EPFL. Since then it has grown a lot.

At the EPFL, people study subjects such as **engineering**, **computer science**, **physics**, **chemistry**, **mathematics** and **architecture**. Many researchers work on new technologies, for example for energy, medicine or robots. New **companies** also come out of the research. The university is known around the world.

The **campus** is in **Ecublens** near Lausanne, very close to **Lake Geneva**. The University of Lausanne is also next to the EPFL. A well-known building is the **Rolex Learning Center**, a library with a wavy floor. Students come here from all over the world.

gewusst: In the Rolex Learning Center at the EPFL, the floor is so wavy that inside you walk up and down little hills.
ETH Zurich and the EPFL are the only two universities that belong directly to the Confederation.

teile.einleitung: FIFA is the world football association. It organises the football World Cups and has its headquarters in Zurich.
wichtigste: FIFA is short for “Fédération Internationale de Football Association”.
FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904.
Since 1932 it has been based in Zurich.
It organises the men's and women's football World Cup.
Over 200 national football associations are members.
There is a FIFA museum in Zurich.

abschnitte.text: **FIFA** is the umbrella organisation of all the national football associations in the world. The name is French and means “International Federation of Association Football”. Together with other bodies, FIFA sets the rules of the game. It also organises big international tournaments. The Swiss Football Association is also a member.

FIFA's best-known tournament is the **football World Cup**. The first one took place in Uruguay in 1930. Since then it has usually been held every four years. Since 1991 there has also been a women's World Cup. The matches are watched on television by a great many people all over the world.

FIFA was founded in **Paris in 1904**. Since **1932**, its headquarters have been in **Zurich**. Today the building stands on the Zürichberg. Switzerland is a popular home for many international sports associations, because the country is neutral and offers good conditions. For example, the International Olympic Committee is also based in Lausanne.

In 2016, a **FIFA museum** opened in Zurich. There you can discover the history of football. You can see, for example, shirts, balls and trophies. There are also games you can join in. The museum is a popular day out for football fans.

gewusst: FIFA has more member associations than the UN has member states.
FIFA has been at home in Zurich for over 90 years.

teile.einleitung: The Gotthard Road Tunnel connects Göschenen in the canton of Uri with Airolo in Ticino. It is about 17 kilometres long and opened in 1980. It is one of the most important road links through the Alps.
wichtigste: The Gotthard Road Tunnel opened in 1980.
It is about 17 kilometres long.
It runs from Göschenen (UR) to Airolo (TI).
It is part of the A2 motorway from Basel to Chiasso.
So far it has only had one tube, with traffic in both directions.
A second tube is being built.

abschnitte.text: Before the tunnel existed, cars had to drive over the **Gotthard Pass**. The pass is high and often closed in winter. With the **road tunnel**, you can drive through under the mountain all year round since **1980**. The tunnel is about 17 kilometres long and belongs to the **A2 motorway**.

The tunnel has only one **tube**. Cars drive in both directions in it, separated only by a centre line. That is why strict rules apply: you have to keep your distance and must not overtake. Lorries are metered, which means they may only enter at certain intervals. On days when many people travel, long **traffic jams** often form in front of the portals.

In **2001**, two lorries collided in the tunnel, and a serious fire broke out in which people died. Safety was improved afterwards. There is a **safety tunnel** next to the main tunnel, shelters and emergency call niches. Since then, lorries have been checked more carefully and metered.

The tunnel has to be thoroughly renovated. So that it does not have to be closed for years while this is done, voters agreed in **2016** to the building of a **second tube**. When it is finished, the old tube will be renewed first. After that, only one direction of travel is to run in each tube, but still only on one lane.

gewusst: Today there are three big tunnels under the Gotthard: the old railway tunnel, the road tunnel and the base tunnel.
When it opened in 1980, the Gotthard Road Tunnel was the longest road tunnel in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Gross-Titlis ski jump is a large ski jump in Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. Every year in December, a Ski Jumping World Cup event takes place there. The best ski jumpers in the world travel there for it.
wichtigste: The Gross-Titlis ski jump stands in Engelberg (OW).
It is a large hill for ski jumping.
A World Cup event takes place there every December.
Thousands of fans watch the jumpers.
The ski jump is named after the mountain Titlis.

abschnitte.text: In **ski jumping**, you first ride down a steep track, the **in-run**, and become very fast. At the end of the track you jump off and fly through the air. The jumpers hold their skis in a V shape so that they stay in the air longer. Points are given for **distance** and for a beautiful, safe jump with a good landing.

In the **World Cup**, the best athletes compete against each other over a whole winter. Engelberg has been a regular stop for many years. The jumps always take place shortly before Christmas. Many **fans** stand at the side of the ski jump, wave flags and cheer on the jumpers. For the Swiss ski jumpers, it is a home event.

abschnitte.titel: At the foot of the Titlis
abschnitte.text: Engelberg lies in a high valley in **Obwalden**, surrounded by high mountains. The best known is the **Titlis**, up which a cable car with a rotating cabin runs. Engelberg is also known for its **monastery**, which was founded as early as the Middle Ages. In winter, many visitors come to ski.

gewusst: On a large hill, the best jumpers fly further than the length of a football pitch.
The Gross-Titlis ski jump is regarded as one of the biggest natural ski jumps in the world, because it is built into a natural slope.

teile.einleitung: The Locarno Film Festival is one of the best-known film festivals in the world. It takes place every year in August in Locarno in the canton of Ticino. The main prize is the Golden Leopard.
wichtigste: The Locarno Film Festival takes place every year in August.
It was held for the first time in 1946.
The main prize is called the Golden Leopard, in Italian “Pardo d'oro”.
In the evenings, films are shown in the open air on the Piazza Grande.
The screen on the Piazza is one of the biggest in Europe.
Locarno lies in the canton of Ticino on Lake Maggiore.

abschnitte.text: The Locarno Film Festival has existed since **1946**. This makes it one of the oldest film festivals in the world. Every year in **August**, filmmakers, experts and many visitors come to Locarno. For about eleven days, hundreds of films from all over the world are shown. Many of them are shown in public for the first time.

What is special is the **Piazza Grande**, the big square in the old town. A huge screen is set up there every evening. Thousands of people sit on chairs in the open air and watch films together. This **open-air cinema** is one of the biggest in Europe. When it rains, many people simply take out their umbrellas.

The symbol of the festival is the **leopard**. All over the city you then see yellow and black leopard patterns. The best film in the competition wins the **Golden Leopard**, in Italian “Pardo d'oro”. There are also other prizes, for example for the best director or for young filmmakers.

Locarno lies in the **canton of Ticino** on the northern shore of **Lake Maggiore**. Italian is spoken here. The warm climate with palm trees and views of the lake makes the town especially popular in summer. The festival brings many visitors to the region every year.

gewusst: About 8,000 people have room on the Piazza Grande for one screening.
During the festival, the whole of Locarno is decorated with yellow and black leopard spots.

teile.einleitung: The Eiger is a famous mountain in the Bernese Oberland. Together with the Mönch and the Jungfrau it forms a trio of peaks that can be seen from far away.
wichtigste: The Eiger is about 3,970 metres high.
The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau stand side by side in the Bernese Oberland.
You can see them well from Grindelwald or Interlaken.
The Eiger North Face is one of the best-known rock walls in the Alps.
It was climbed for the first time in 1938.
The Jungfrau Railway runs through a tunnel inside the Eiger and the Mönch.

abschnitte.text: In the **Bernese Oberland**, three well-known mountains stand side by side: the **Eiger**, the **Mönch** and the **Jungfrau**. The Eiger is about **3,970 metres** high, while the Mönch and the Jungfrau are both over 4,000 metres high. You can see them especially well from **Grindelwald**, **Interlaken** or **Kleine Scheidegg**. The picture of the three peaks can be seen on many postcards.

The **North Face** of the Eiger is about 1,800 metres high and very steep. It is considered one of the most difficult and best-known walls in the Alps. In **1938**, a rope team of four climbers managed to climb all the way up it for the first time. Because of falling rocks and sudden changes in the weather, the wall is still dangerous today.

The **Jungfrau Railway** runs from Kleine Scheidegg through a long **tunnel** inside the Eiger and the Mönch. Its destination is the **Jungfraujoch**, at over 3,400 metres. The highest railway station in Europe is there. The railway was finished in 1912.

The area around the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** “Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch”. The **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the largest glacier in the Alps, is also found there. The World Heritage Site protects this special high mountain landscape. Every year, a great many visitors come from all over the world.

gewusst: An old tale says that the Mönch (“monk”) stands between the Eiger and the Jungfrau (“maiden”) to protect her.
The Jungfraujoch station is at over 3,400 metres and is the highest railway station in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Gottlieber Hüppen are thin, rolled wafer tubes from Gottlieben in the canton of Thurgau. They are crisp and often filled with a sweet cream. All over Switzerland they are known as a fine pastry.
wichtigste: Gottlieber Hüppen come from Gottlieben in Thurgau.
They are thin, rolled wafers.
They are often filled with chocolate or praline.
Gottlieben lies on the Seerhein between Lake Constance and the Untersee.
The Hüppen are sold in tins and are often given as presents.

abschnitte.text: A **Hüppe** is a very thin wafer. The batter is baked wafer-thin and rolled into a tube while it is still warm. As it cools, the wafer becomes crisp. The tubes are then filled with a cream, for example made of **chocolate** or **praline**. You eat them with coffee, as a dessert or simply as a treat.

**Gottlieben** is a small village in the canton of **Thurgau**. It lies on the **Seerhein**, the short stretch of the Rhine between Lake Constance and the Untersee. The village has lovely old half-timbered houses and a **castle**. Right opposite, on the other side of the Rhine, lies Germany.

The Hüppen carry the name of the place they come from. They are made in Gottlieben and sold in pretty **tins**. Many people buy them as a souvenir or a present. This is how a very small village has become known all over Switzerland.

gewusst: Gottlieben is one of the smallest municipalities in the canton of Thurgau.
Hüppen are baked so thin that you can almost see through them.

teile.einleitung: Lake Hallwil is a lake in the Seetal valley in the canton of Aargau. Its southern end reaches into the canton of Lucerne. In summer you can swim there, take a boat trip and walk along the shore.
wichtigste: Lake Hallwil lies in the Seetal valley in the canton of Aargau.
A small part in the south belongs to the canton of Lucerne.
It is the largest lake that lies almost entirely in Aargau.
Hallwyl moated castle stands at the northern end.
In summer, scheduled boats cross the lake.
In many places the shore is a nature reserve.

abschnitte.text: The **Seetal** (“Lake Valley”) is a long valley between Aargau and Lucerne. Two lakes lie in it: **Lake Baldegg** and the larger **Lake Hallwil**. Both were shaped by a glacier in the Ice Age. On the shore of Lake Hallwil there are villages such as Meisterschwanden, Seengen and Beinwil am See.

At the northern end of the lake stands **Hallwyl Castle**. It is a **moated castle**, which means it is surrounded by water-filled moats and stands on islands. The noble family of Hallwyl lived here for many centuries. Today the castle is a **museum** where you can learn about life in earlier times.

In summer, Lake Hallwil is a popular place to visit. There are **lidos**, sailing boats and **scheduled boats** that link the villages on the shore. A walking path leads around the lake. In winter, in very cold years, the lake sometimes freezes over.

In the past, many **nutrients** from fertiliser and waste water got into the lake. As a result, too many algae grew, and the fish in the depths lacked **oxygen**. With sewage treatment plants and artificial aeration, the lake became healthier again. Many stretches of shore are a **nature reserve**, so that birds and plants have a habitat.

gewusst: The river Aabach flows out of Lake Hallwil and past Hallwyl Castle.
Rare plants and many water birds live in the reedbeds on the shore.

teile.einleitung: The Höllgrotten are dripstone caves near Baar in the canton of Zug. They lie in the Lorzentobel, a narrow gorge of the river Lorze, and can be visited.
wichtigste: The Höllgrotten lie in the Lorzentobel near Baar in the canton of Zug.
They are dripstone caves with many glittering lime formations.
They were discovered in the 19th century while tufa stone was being quarried.
The formations grew over thousands of years.
Today a circular path leads through several cave chambers.

abschnitte.text: The Höllgrotten are in the **Lorzentobel**, where the Lorze has cut deep into the land. The caves are not very big, but they are richly decorated. Visitors walk along a path through several chambers. Lamps light up the formations so that they can be seen well. Inside, it is cool and damp all year round.

Rainwater seeps through the ground and dissolves **lime** from the rock as it goes. When the water drips from the ceiling in the cave, a tiny bit of lime stays behind. In this way **stalactites** grow downwards from above and **stalagmites** grow upwards from the floor. This is very slow, often only millimetres in many years. That is why the formations in the Höllgrotten are thousands of years old.

The caves were discovered in the 19th century when workers were quarrying **tufa stone** on the slope. Tufa is a porous limestone that used to be popular for building. Soon people noticed how beautiful the hollows were. So they were opened to visitors. Since then, the Höllgrotten have been a popular place to visit in the canton of Zug.

gewusst: Stalactites hang from the ceiling, stalagmites grow from the floor. When they meet, a column forms.
The Höllgrotten are among the best-known show caves in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Fête des Vendanges is the big wine growers' festival of the city of Neuchâtel. It takes place every year at the end of September and celebrates the end of the grape harvest.
wichtigste: The Fête des Vendanges takes place every year in Neuchâtel.
It is celebrated on the last weekend in September.
“Vendanges” means “grape harvest” in English.
The highlight is a big parade with decorated floats.
There is a lot of music, including Guggenmusik bands.
The festival is one of the biggest popular festivals in French-speaking Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: A festival for the grape harvest
abschnitte.text: In autumn, the ripe **grapes** are picked in the vineyards. This harvest is called the **grape harvest**, in French “vendanges”. There are many vineyards around **Lake Neuchâtel**. At the end of the grape harvest, the city of **Neuchâtel** holds a big festival, the **Fête des Vendanges**. It always takes place on the last weekend in September.

The highlight of the festival is the **parade** on Sunday, in French “Corso fleuri”. Floats magnificently decorated with **flowers** move through the streets. **Bands** and Guggenmusik groups play along. Thousands of spectators stand at the side of the road. There is also a parade of its own for children.

For three days, the old town of Neuchâtel is full of stalls, stages and music. Many clubs sell food and drinks. The festival has been celebrated for many decades. Every year it attracts visitors from all over Switzerland. Neuchâtel is the main town of the canton of the same name, where French is spoken.

gewusst: The floats in the Fête des Vendanges parade are decorated with thousands of real flowers.

teile.einleitung: The Glasi Hergiswil is a glassworks in Hergiswil in the canton of Nidwalden. Glass is still blown by hand there. Visitors can watch the glassblowers at work.
wichtigste: The Glasi lies in Hergiswil on Lake Lucerne.
Glass is blown and shaped by hand there.
You can watch the glassblowers at work.
The glassworks has existed since the 19th century.
A museum and a shop belong to the Glasi.

abschnitte.text: Glass consists mainly of **quartz sand**, with other substances such as soda and lime added. In a furnace, everything is melted at very high heat until a glowing, sticky mass is formed. The **glassblower** picks some of it up on a long tube, the **blowpipe**. Then he blows into it, turns and shapes the glass until, for example, a vase or a drinking glass is made.

Glass has been made in Hergiswil since the **19th century**. Like many small glassworks, this one ran into difficulties because factories make glass more cheaply with machines. In the 1970s, the glass artist **Roberto Niederer** took over the Glasi and focused on handwork and designs of its own. This allowed it to carry on.

Today the Glasi is a popular **place to visit**. In the workshop you can see how a finished piece is made from glowing mass. A **museum** tells the history of glassmaking. For children there are play areas all about glass. Hergiswil is easy to reach from Lucerne by train and boat.

gewusst: Molten glass is so hot that it glows red and orange.
Finished glass has to cool down slowly, otherwise it can crack.

teile.einleitung: The Fondation Beyeler is a famous art museum in Riehen in the canton of Basel-Stadt. It shows works by great modern artists in a bright building in the middle of a park.
wichtigste: The Fondation Beyeler is in Riehen in the canton of Basel-Stadt.
It was founded by the art dealers Ernst and Hildy Beyeler.
The museum opened in 1997.
The Italian architect Renzo Piano designed the building.
The collection includes works by Monet, Cézanne, Picasso and many others.
It is one of the most visited art museums in Switzerland.

abschnitte.titel: A museum made from a collection
abschnitte.text: **Ernst and Hildy Beyeler** were art dealers in Basel. Over many years they collected important paintings and sculptures. Later they set up a **foundation**, in French “fondation”. So that their collection would be open to everyone, they had a museum of their own built. It opened in **1997**.

The museum was designed by the famous Italian architect **Renzo Piano**. The long, low building has a glass roof that lets plenty of **daylight** into the rooms. It lies in a beautiful **park** with old trees. In front of the museum there is a pond with water lilies, which recalls the water lily paintings by Claude Monet.

The collection includes works of **classical modernism**, that is art mostly from the 19th and 20th centuries. These include paintings by **Claude Monet**, **Paul Cézanne**, **Vincent van Gogh** and **Pablo Picasso**. Sculptures by the Swiss artist **Alberto Giacometti** can also be seen. The museum also puts on big special exhibitions from time to time.

The canton of **Basel-Stadt** consists of only three municipalities: Basel, **Riehen** and Bettingen. Riehen lies right on the border with Germany. The tram runs from Basel to right in front of the museum. Many visitors also come to Riehen from abroad.

gewusst: So much daylight comes in through the museum's glass roof that you often see the paintings almost as if you were outdoors.
With only three municipalities, Basel-Stadt is the canton with the fewest municipalities in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Fricktal is a region in the north of the canton of Aargau, right on the Rhine. For centuries it belonged to Austria and only became part of the canton of Aargau in 1803.
wichtigste: The Fricktal lies in the north of the canton of Aargau.
In the north, the Rhine forms the border with Germany.
For centuries the Fricktal belonged to Further Austria.
Further Austria was a territory ruled by the Habsburgs.
In 1803 the Fricktal became part of the new canton of Aargau.
Dinosaur bones were found in Frick.

abschnitte.text: The **Fricktal** lies in the north of the canton of **Aargau**, between the Jura and the **Rhine**. Here the Rhine forms the border with **Germany**. The districts of Rheinfelden and Laufenburg belong to the Fricktal. Important places include Rheinfelden, Laufenburg and Frick. The landscape is hilly, with forests, fields and many fruit trees.

For a long time, the Fricktal was not part of the Swiss Confederation. It was part of **Further Austria**. This was the name for the lands of the **Habsburgs** in the west, far away from Vienna. So for centuries the people of the Fricktal had an Austrian ruler. That is why the region is still mostly Catholic today.

Around **1800**, Europe changed greatly because of the wars with France. Austria had to give up the Fricktal. For a short time there was even a **canton of Fricktal** of its own. In **1803**, the area then became part of the newly founded **canton of Aargau**. Since then it has belonged to Switzerland.

In a clay pit near **Frick**, many bones of **dinosaurs** were found, mostly of **Plateosaurus**. These plant-eaters lived over 200 million years ago. At the **Frick Dinosaur Museum** you can marvel at the finds. The Fricktal is also known for its **cherries**.

gewusst: So many Plateosaurus fossils have been found in the Fricktal that it is one of the most important sites for these dinosaurs in Europe.
There are two towns called Rheinfelden: one on the Swiss side and one on the German side of the Rhine.

teile.einleitung: The Eringer is a breed of cattle from the Valais. The cows are small, strong and dark, and they like to test their strength against each other. This is how the well-known cow fights came about.
wichtigste: The Eringer is an old breed of cattle from the Valais.
The name comes from the Eringer valley, in French the Val d'Hérens.
The cows are rather small, strong and mostly dark brown to black.
They measure their strength by pushing their heads against each other.
At the cow fights, the strongest cow is crowned queen.
The breed is well suited to life in the mountains.

abschnitte.text: The **Eringer** is an old **breed of cattle** from the **Valais**. Its name comes from the **Eringer valley**, in French the **Val d'Hérens**, a side valley near Sion. The animals are rather small, but very **strong**. Their coat is mostly dark brown to black, and they have short, strong horns.

Eringer cows are well suited to life in the **mountains**. They can walk safely on steep pastures and manage with simple feed. In summer, many of them spend their time on the **alp**. Farmers keep them for **milk** and **meat**.

Eringer cows have a strong will and want to settle their rank in the herd. To do this, they push their **heads** against each other and shove. The cow that gives up and runs away has lost. This natural behaviour led to the **cow fights**, in French **Combats de reines**.

At the cow fights, cows compete against each other in different **categories**. The strongest cow is crowned **queen** and often receives a big bell. In spring there are fights in several places in the Valais and a big **final**. In summer, the queen often also leads the herd on the alp.

For many people in the Valais, the cow fights are an important **tradition** and a popular festival. Supporters say that the cows are only showing their natural behaviour. Animal welfare groups make sure the animals are well looked after. There are therefore rules to make the fights as safe as possible for the cows.

gewusst: Only cows fight at the cow fights, no bulls.
The queen of a herd is called “reine” in French.

teile.einleitung: At 991 metres, the Hohgrat is the highest point in the canton of Thurgau. It lies in the south of the canton near Fischingen. Thurgau is hilly, but it has no really high mountains.
wichtigste: The Hohgrat is 991 metres high.
It is the highest point in the canton of Thurgau.
It lies in the south of the canton near Fischingen.
The area is called the Hinterthurgau.
Thurgau has hills, but no Alpine peaks.

abschnitte.titel: A hill as the highest point
abschnitte.text: At **991 metres** above sea level, the **Hohgrat** is the highest point in **Thurgau**. Compared with the Alps this is not much, and many Alpine peaks are three times as high. The Hohgrat is wooded and is more a long ridge of hills than a pointed peak. It is easy to reach on walking trails.

The Hohgrat lies in the **Hinterthurgau**, the southern and hilliest part of the canton. Nearby is **Fischingen** with its well-known **monastery**. In the north, Thurgau is flatter and reaches as far as **Lake Constance**. There are many fruit trees there, which is why Thurgau is also called “Mostindien” (“Cider India”).

abschnitte.titel: The highest points of the cantons
abschnitte.text: Every canton has a **highest point**. In mountain cantons such as Valais or Graubünden, these are peaks over 4,000 metres. In cantons of the Central Plateau such as Thurgau, Zurich or Aargau, they are hills and mountains under 1,300 metres. The canton with the lowest highest point is Basel-Stadt.

gewusst: The highest point in Switzerland is the Dufourspitze at 4,634 metres, almost five times as high as the Hohgrat.
Because of its many apple trees, Thurgau is jokingly called “Mostindien”.

teile.einleitung: Glarus is the main town of the canton of Glarus. The canton and its main town have the same name. Glarus is especially known for the Landsgemeinde, where those entitled to vote cast their votes in the open air.
wichtigste: Glarus is the main town of the canton of the same name.
The town lies in the valley of the Linth, at the foot of the Glärnisch.
Every year in May the Landsgemeinde takes place in Glarus.
In 1861 a great fire destroyed most of the town.
After that, Glarus was rebuilt with straight streets at right angles.
Since 2011 the canton of Glarus has had only three municipalities.

abschnitte.text: Glarus lies in the **Glarus region**, a valley shaped by the river **Linth**. The mighty **Glärnisch** rises right above the town. The mountains are so close that on some days in winter the sun shines only briefly. Glarus is well connected by train to Zurich and Lake Walen.

On the first Sunday in May, those entitled to vote gather on the **Zaunplatz** in Glarus. At the **Landsgemeinde**, they vote by raising their hands instead of putting a slip of paper in a ballot box. This is how laws are passed and offices are filled. Apart from Glarus, only Appenzell Innerrhoden still has this old form of direct democracy.

In May **1861**, a fire broke out in Glarus. A strong foehn wind drove the flames through the town, and a large part of the houses burned down. After that, Glarus was planned anew: since then, the streets have run straight and at right angles, almost like a **chessboard**. You can still see this today when you walk through the town.

In the past, the canton of Glarus had over twenty municipalities. The Landsgemeinde decided to merge them into just three municipalities. Since **2011** there have been **Glarus Nord**, **Glarus** and **Glarus Süd**. Since then, Netstal, Ennenda and Riedern have also belonged to the municipality of Glarus. No other canton has so few municipalities.

gewusst: The Glarus cantonal flag shows Saint Fridolin, a wanderer with a staff and a Bible.
Glarus used to be an important centre of the textile industry, known for printed fabrics.

teile.einleitung: Herisau is the largest municipality in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. The cantonal government and the cantonal parliament have their seat here. Herisau lies in a hilly landscape not far from St Gallen.
wichtigste: Herisau is the largest municipality in Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
The government and the cantonal parliament have their seat here.
The cantonal court, however, is in Trogen.
Herisau lies close to the city of St Gallen.
In the past, Herisau was an important centre of the textile industry.

abschnitte.text: Appenzell Ausserrhoden does not have a single main town in the usual sense. In **Herisau**, the **Regierungsrat** (government) and the **Kantonsrat** (parliament) meet. The court is in **Trogen**. This division has to do with the history of the canton, in which various villages were important. Herisau is nevertheless regarded as the main town of the canton.

Herisau is the municipality with the most inhabitants in the canton. In the centre there are beautiful old **Appenzell houses** and the Reformed church. Around the town lie hills with farms and woods. Herisau has a railway station where several railway lines cross.

In the 18th and 19th centuries, many **fabrics** were made and traded in Herisau. The **textile industry** brought work and prosperity to the region. Wealthy merchants built magnificent houses that can still be seen today. Later, other businesses appeared, and today many people also work in nearby St Gallen.

gewusst: Appenzell Ausserrhoden abolished the Landsgemeinde in 1997, and today votes are held at the ballot box.
In Herisau there is the Herisau Museum, which shows the history of the municipality.

teile.einleitung: In Réclère in the canton of Jura there are dripstone caves, the Grottes de Réclère. There you can marvel at stalactites and stalagmites that have grown over a very long time. Right next to them is a park with large models of dinosaurs.
wichtigste: The Grottes de Réclère are in the canton of Jura.
They are dripstone caves.
Stalactites hang from the ceiling, stalagmites grow up from the floor.
Dripstones grow very slowly from water containing lime.
Next to the caves there is a park with dinosaur models.

abschnitte.text: Rainwater seeps through the ground and the **limestone**. As it does so, it dissolves a little lime. When the water drips from the ceiling of a cave, a tiny bit of lime stays behind. In this way, over a very long time, a spike grows down from the ceiling, the **stalactite**. Where the drops fall on the floor, a **stalagmite** grows upwards. When the two meet, a column forms.

The caves of **Réclère** are in the **Ajoie**, in the far north-west of the canton of Jura, near the border with France. The caves were discovered in the 19th century. Today a lit tour leads through the underground passages. In the cave it is cool and damp all year round, so it is worth taking a jacket.

Next to the caves there is a park where life-size **models of dinosaurs** and other prehistoric animals stand in the forest. There you can find out how these animals lived many millions of years ago. For children especially, the combination of a cave and a prehistoric park makes an exciting day out.

gewusst: A dripstone often grows only a few millimetres in a hundred years.
A way to remember: stalactites hang from the ceiling, stalagmites stand on the ground.

teile.einleitung: Fribourg, in German Freiburg im Üechtland, is the main town of the canton of Fribourg. The city has a beautiful medieval old town and lies exactly on the language border between German and French.
wichtigste: Fribourg is the main town of the canton of Fribourg.
In German the city is called Freiburg.
It was founded in 1157 by the Dukes of Zähringen.
The city is bilingual, and most people speak French.
The river Saane flows in loops around the old town.
The Cathedral of St Nicholas is the landmark.

abschnitte.text: Fribourg was founded in **1157** by **Berthold IV of Zähringen**. The Zähringens also founded other towns, for example Bern. The addition “im Üechtland” in the German name distinguishes the city from Freiburg im Breisgau in Germany. In **1481**, Fribourg joined the Swiss Confederation.

Fribourg lies exactly on the **language border**. Most people speak **French**, but many also speak **German**. The river **Saane**, in French Sarine, is often seen as the border between the two language areas. That is why people sometimes talk about the “Röstigraben” (the “rösti ditch”). The **University of Fribourg** is also bilingual.

The **old town** is one of the biggest medieval old towns in Switzerland. It lies high above the loops of the Saane. Old **bridges**, some of them made of wood, cross the river. The landmark is the **Cathedral of St Nicholas** with its tall tower. From the top you have a wide view over the rooftops.

Since 1899, a **funicular railway** has run in Fribourg between the lower town and the upper town. What is special is that it is driven by **waste water** from the city. One car is filled with water at the top and, with its weight, pulls the other car up. This technique is very rare today.

gewusst: The Fribourg funicular runs on waste water and is one of the last of its kind in Europe.
The University of Fribourg is the only bilingual university in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Geneva Conventions are international treaties that are meant to protect people in wars. They are named after the city of Geneva, where the first convention was signed in 1864.
wichtigste: The Geneva Conventions protect the wounded, prisoners and civilians in wars.
The first Geneva Convention was signed in 1864.
The impetus came from Henry Dunant of Geneva.
The four conventions in force today date from 1949.
Almost all the states in the world have accepted them.
Switzerland keeps the treaties.

abschnitte.text: Even in a war there are **rules**. The most important ones are in the **Geneva Conventions**. They require that the **wounded** are cared for, no matter which side they fought on. **Prisoners** must be treated humanely. And **civilians**, people who are not fighting, are to be protected. These rules are also called **international humanitarian law**.

The impetus came from the Geneva businessman **Henry Dunant**. In 1859 he came to a battlefield at **Solferino** in northern Italy. He saw that many wounded men were left without help, and he organised help with volunteers. Afterwards he wrote a book about it. In 1863 this led to the founding of the **International Committee of the Red Cross** in Geneva. In 1901, Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.

The **first Geneva Convention** was signed by several states in Geneva in **1864**. Further treaties were added later. After the Second World War, four new conventions were agreed in **1949**, and they still apply today. In 1977, additional protocols were added. Today **almost all the states in the world** have accepted the conventions.

**Switzerland** is the state that keeps the originals of the treaties. It is therefore called the **depositary state**. The **red cross** on a white background is the protective emblem of the conventions. It is the Swiss flag with the colours reversed, as a tribute to Switzerland. The International Committee of the Red Cross still has its headquarters in Geneva.

gewusst: The Red Cross emblem is the Swiss flag with the colours swapped.
The Geneva Conventions are among the few treaties that have been accepted by almost all the states in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Einsiedeln Schafbock is a traditional biscuit from Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz. It is a honey gingerbread biscuit that is shaped in wooden moulds.
wichtigste: The Schafbock is a speciality from Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It is a gingerbread biscuit made with honey.
The dough is pressed into carved wooden moulds.
The picture often shows a ram.
Einsiedeln is a well-known place of pilgrimage with a large monastery.

abschnitte.text: The **Einsiedeln Schafböcke** are a flat, firm biscuit made from **gingerbread dough** with **honey**. The dough is pressed into **wooden moulds**. These are wooden forms with a picture carved into them. After baking, you can see the picture as a relief on the biscuit, often a **ram** (“Schafbock”).

**Einsiedeln** in the canton of **Schwyz** has been an important **place of pilgrimage** since the Middle Ages. Many pilgrims visit the **monastery** with the Black Madonna. From early on, they bought biscuits as a souvenir for their families at home. This is how the Schafböcke became known far and wide.

You can still buy the Schafböcke in the **bakeries** of Einsiedeln today. Some bakeries still use old, beautifully carved **moulds** for them. The biscuit is quite hard and keeps for a long time. Many visitors take it home as a **souvenir**.

gewusst: Some of the wooden moulds for the Schafböcke are very old and are kept like little works of art.

teile.einleitung: The Franches-Montagnes horse (known in German as the Freiberger) comes from the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura. It is strong, calm and friendly and is regarded as the last native horse breed of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Franches-Montagnes horse comes from the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura.
In German the area is called the Freiberge.
It is regarded as the last native horse breed of Switzerland.
These horses are strong, calm and versatile.
They are used as riding horses and as draught horses.
The National Stud Farm in Avenches looks after the breeding.

abschnitte.text: The **Franches-Montagnes horse** is a **breed of horse** from Switzerland. It is named after the **Franches-Montagnes**, a high plateau in the canton of **Jura**. In German the area is called “Freiberge”. Horses have been bred there for a long time. The Franches-Montagnes horse is regarded as the last original horse breed of Switzerland.

These horses are medium-sized and **strong**, with powerful legs. Most have a brown coat or are chestnuts with a reddish coat. They have a **calm and friendly** character. That is why they are also well suited to children and beginners. They have plenty of stamina and cope well with the harsh climate in the Jura.

These horses are very **versatile**. In the past they mainly helped on farms and pulled carts and ploughs. The Swiss Army also used them as draught animals for a long time. Today they are used as **riding horses**, as **carriage horses** and for leisure. Sometimes they even still work in the forest, pulling tree trunks.

Every year in August, the **Marché-Concours** takes place in **Saignelégier**. This is a big festival all about the Franches-Montagnes horse. There are horse shows, parades and races. The breed is also supported by the Confederation at the **National Stud Farm** in **Avenches** in the canton of Vaud. On the pastures of the Franches-Montagnes, you often see the horses grazing freely among the fir trees.

gewusst: In the Franches-Montagnes, horses often graze on open pastures between single fir trees, the so-called wooded pastures (“Wytweiden”).
The Marché-Concours in Saignelégier has been held for over a hundred years.

teile.einleitung: The Glarner Pastete is a sweet pastry from the canton of Glarus. It is made of crisp puff pastry and has a filling of almonds and plums. Throughout Switzerland it is regarded as a typical speciality of Glarus.
wichtigste: The Glarner Pastete is a speciality from the canton of Glarus.
It is made of puff pastry.
It is filled with almond paste and plum purée.
The pastry is round and nicely decorated on top.
You can buy it in bakeries and confectioners' shops in the Glarus region.

abschnitte.text: The case of the pastry is made of **puff pastry**. This dough consists of many thin layers of dough and butter. When it bakes, the layers rise and become crisp. Inside is a filling of **almond paste** and **plum purée**. This makes the pastry taste nutty and fruity at the same time.

abschnitte.titel: A piece of the Glarus region
abschnitte.text: The canton of **Glarus** lies in a narrow valley between high mountains. Many regions of Switzerland have a typical pastry of their own, and for Glarus it is the Pastete. Bakeries in the canton make it and also sell it as a gift. Anyone who visits the Glarus region often takes a Pastete home.

Besides the Pastete, Glarus is also known for **Schabziger**, a spicy herb cheese. Such **regional specialities** have often been made for many generations using old recipes. They are part of the culture of a canton, like customs or dialects. That is why they are gladly looked after in Switzerland.

gewusst: Puff pastry often has several hundred wafer-thin layers.
Schabziger from Glarus gets its greenish colour from a herb called blue fenugreek (“Schabzigerklee”).

teile.einleitung: The Étang de la Gruère is a moorland pond in the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura. It is surrounded by forest and raised bog and is a nature reserve.
wichtigste: The Étang de la Gruère lies in the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura.
“Étang” is the French word for pond.
The water is dark in colour because of the peat.
A protected raised bog lies around the pond.
In the past the pond was dammed to run a mill.

abschnitte.text: The Étang de la Gruère lies on the high plateau of the **Franches-Montagnes**, in the canton of **Jura**. The pond is surrounded by spruces, birches and mountain pines. A **raised bog** spreads out around the water. A raised bog is very wet ground that is fed only by rain.
